subject: Food Science
title: How Digestion Works
description: A quick win: understand How Digestion Works.

hook.text: Your digestive system is a 9-meter tube running from mouth to anus. Food takes 24–72 hours to complete the journey.

buildup.text: Digestion starts in the mouth: teeth grind food while amylase in saliva begins breaking starch into sugar.

discovery.text: The stomach is a pH 2 acid bath—strong enough to dissolve metal. It kills bacteria and unfolds proteins for enzyme access.

twist.text: Most nutrient absorption happens in the small intestine, not the stomach. Its 7-meter folded surface area equals a tennis court.

climax.text: The large intestine absorbs water and houses trillions of bacteria that ferment fiber and produce vitamins B and K.

punchline.text: Mouth grinds. Stomach dissolves. Small intestine absorbs. Large intestine recycles.

quiz.question: Where does most nutrient absorption occur?
options: The small intestine—its folded surface equals a tennis court
